How it works

Systems, ownership and access
Ticketing + Wi-Fi

A known identity and usable permission are distinct. Each source needs a documented consent field and capture context.

Campaign forms

A form or social campaign becomes a consent source only through its actual form/export and captured permission evidence.

Manual population

A manual list can supply population evidence. It is not automatically a dated opt-in action.

Identity and evidence

Preserve source identity and action times. Joining a source record does not manufacture consent.

Franchise rules

Fictional branches may resolve authority differently. A dated event policy and a conservative negative-precedence policy are different contracts.

Changed customer rows

A customer-feed export carries the agreed fields and permission result. Transfer success is not proof of final audience membership.

Enhanced FTP → import

File delivery and import are separate steps. The receiving import must be checked independently.

Access: SFMC automation owner and Enhanced FTP administrator

Preferences

SFMC preferences may be transformed or merged downstream of the incoming customer feed. The business owner defines their meaning.

Final audience

Selection combines audience rules and permitted use. Native unsubscribe/held state is another sending control.

Owner: Marketing / SFMC

Preference actions

Return an authoritative status and action time. Apply it in the warehouse before the next feed is derived.

The warehouse expects 1,200 members. The next transfer contains 35 new members. The campaign destination starts with 1,177 members, including 14 retained from an older audience.

Rules and supporting detail

The complete loop

Source records
→
Audience rules
→
Campaign destination
→
Response events
↩
Return to the next audience

Response events → stored consent changes → audience rules → next campaign selection

Audience rules select eligible people. A transfer updates the campaign destination. A separate comparison reconciles membership. Opens, clicks, and withdrawals return through an event feed; the next audience changes only after the relevant rule consumes them.

Consent and audience membership answer different questions. A person may belong to a segment and still be ineligible for a particular message.

How the example handles privacy

All counts and records are synthetic. The controls update an in-memory model and send no campaign, export, or personal information.
